system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation: heat transfer resistance equation (1/U_total = 1/h_fouling + 1/h_clean). Fouling resistance increases over time, reducing U. Target U > 2500 W/m2K requires keeping fouling resistance < 0.0004 m2K/W. USER CONSTRAINT: 2500 W/m2K minimum U-value for 12 months without chlorination >0.5 ppm.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 1) Install pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment unit with titanium electrodes (corrosion-resistant) upstream of heat exchanger. 2) Set PEF parameters: 20 kV/cm electric field strength, 100 μs pulse width, 100 Hz frequency. 3) Install flow cell with appropriate residence time (0.5 seconds). 4) Use power supply with energy input <0.1 kWh/m3. 5) Monitor pressure drop across heat exchanger with differential pressure transmitters (0-2 bar range, ±0.1% accuracy). 6) Clean-in-place (CIP) system with citric acid for periodic maintenance. OFF-THE-SHELF components except custom PEF chamber.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Standard practice uses mechanical cleaning every 3-6 months with chlorination. This PEF approach has higher initial cost (~$15k vs $5k for standard) but eliminates chlorination costs and extends cleaning interval to 12 months. Operability is comparable (automated system), maintenance is similar (electrode replacement every 5 years). Worth the premium due to elimination of chlorination byproducts and reduced downtime.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install PEF unit upstream of heat exchanger. Run district cooling loop at design flow rate (1000 L/min) and temperature (inlet 6°C, outlet 12°C). Monitor differential pressure across heat exchanger and heat transfer coefficient weekly for 12 months. Instruments: calibrated temperature sensors (±0.1°C), flow meter (±1%), differential pressure transmitters (±0.1%), power analyzer. PASS threshold: ΔP increase <20% from baseline and U-value >2500 W/m2K throughout 12 months. FAIL threshold: ΔP increase >20% or U-value <2500 W/m2K at any point. Duration: 12 months continuous operation. ASSUMPTION: District cooling water has typical conductivity (500 μS/cm) and microbial load (10^3 CFU/mL).
